title: HTTP/HTTPS
subtitle: Stateless request-response semantics, method idempotency, status code taxonomy, caching headers, and TLS-secured transport.
keyTakeaways: HTTP is an application-layer stateless protocol where every request contains all metadata (headers, method, URI, auth) required for the server to process it.
HTTP methods carry formal semantics: `GET`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` are idempotent by specification, whereas `POST` is non-idempotent and `PATCH` is typically non-idempotent.
HTTPS wraps HTTP inside a TLS encrypted tunnel, guaranteeing Confidentiality (encryption), Integrity (MAC/AEAD prevents tampering), and Authenticity (X.509 certificates).

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) is the foundational request-response protocol of the web. Because HTTP is stateless, any horizontal backend replica can service any request without remembering prior packets. Adhering strictly to HTTP method semantics and status codes enables intermediaries, CDNs, reverse proxies, browser caches, and API gateways, to automatically cache, retry, or circuit-break traffic without inspecting application business logic.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: HTTP is an application-layer stateless protocol where every request contains all metadata (headers, method, URI, auth) required for the server to process it.

**Problem Space & Invariants**: HTTP methods carry formal semantics: `GET`, `PUT`, and `DELETE` are idempotent by specification, whereas `POST` is non-idempotent and `PATCH` is typically non-idempotent.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for HTTP/HTTPS:
bullets: **End-to-End HTTPS / mTLS (Client -> LB -> Pod)**: Provides zero-trust encryption even inside the vpc, cryptographic service identity verification via client certs, soc2/pci compliance. Best suited for Fintech, healthcare (HIPAA), multi-tenant cloud infrastructure, and zero-trust microservice meshes.

**TLS Termination at Edge Load Balancer (HTTPS -> LB -> Plain HTTP)**: Provides offloads tls handshake cpu and cert management to a single gateway/alb tier, simplifies internal debugging and packet capture. Best suited for Standard single-VPC startups and low-sensitivity internal backends inside isolated private subnets.
Safe & Idempotent Methods: `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS` (read-only, safe for automatic proxy retries and prefetching).
Idempotent Mutating Methods: `PUT` (full resource replacement) and `DELETE` (repeating `DELETE /items/5` yields the same system state).
HSTS (`Strict-Transport-Security`): Instructs browsers to never attempt plaintext port 80 connections, preventing SSL-stripping attacks.
HTTP Compression (`Accept-Encoding: br, zstd, gzip`): Compresses JSON/HTML payloads by 70-85% over the wire.

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply HTTP/HTTPS across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Fintech, healthcare (HIPAA), multi-tenant cloud infrastructure, and zero-trust microservice meshes, suited for environments requiring Zero-trust encryption even inside the VPC, cryptographic service identity verification via client certs, SOC2/PCI compliance.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Standard single-VPC startups and low-sensitivity internal backends inside isolated private subnets, where Offloads TLS handshake CPU and cert management to a single gateway/ALB tier, simplifies internal debugging and packet capture.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: Plaintext HTTP is vulnerable to passive eavesdropping and active Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) header/body injection across ISP routers and Wi-Fi access points. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of HTTP/HTTPS introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: extra cpu overhead for tls encryption/decryption on every internal hop, certificate rotation complexity (requires istio/linkerd/cert-manager).

**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: traffic inside the private vpc subnet travels unencrypted; vulnerable if an attacker breaches the internal network perimeter.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for HTTP/HTTPS:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: HTTPS wraps HTTP inside a TLS encrypted tunnel, guaranteeing Confidentiality (encryption), Integrity (MAC/AEAD prevents tampering), and Authenticity (X.509 certificates).

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Don't overlook HTTP `ETag` and `Cache-Control: stale-while-revalidate` headers in interviews: mentioning them shows how you eliminate 80% of backend bandwidth before requests ever leave the CDN or browser.
